opportunities.title: Propose vulnerability identity key and lifecycle schema
opportunities.summary: ### Summary Inspect the committed Anchore JSON fixtures and propose a schema for tracking vulnerabilities over time. Specifically: what combination of fields uniquely identifies "the same vulnerability" across scans? Candidates to evaluate include CVE ID alone, CVE + package name, CVE + package name + version, and CVE + package + image. Write up the tradeoffs, pick a recommendation, and sketch the analytics DB table(s) needed to support first_seen / last_seen / fixed_at / ignored_at / cleared_at fields. **Tech notes:** The Anchore JSON schema is documented at the Anchore project site; worth skimming before diving into fixtures. The goal of this spike is a decision, not code — resist the urge to start implementing. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Written proposal (markdown doc in PR) covering identity key options, tradeoffs, and a recommendation - [ ] Proposed analytics DB schema with column types and rationale - [ ] At least one worked example from the fixtures showing how the identity key behaves across days - [ ] Reviewed and approved by Brandon and/or Matt before next ticket starts ## Bounty: $250 This issue has been selected for our paid contributor program. opportunities.title: [MCP] HTTP proxy support for Remote MCP behind corporate firewalls
opportunities.summary: ## Context mcp-remote provides `--enable-proxy` to respect `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables. MisakaNet Remote MCP has no proxy awareness — agents behind corporate firewalls cannot reach `misakanet.org/mcp`. ## Why - Enterprise adoption: many corporate environments require HTTP proxy for outbound connections - China mainland: some networks need proxy to reach Cloudflare CDN reliably - Self-hosted: users running MisakaNet Worker on internal networks may need proxy for KV/GitHub API ## Proposed design For the Cloudflare Worker (server-side): not applicable — Workers run on Cloudflare edge, no proxy needed. For client-side integration (agents, CLI, SDK): 1. Document `HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` support in README 2. In `misaka capture` CLI and any future SDK, respect proxy env vars: ```python import urllib.request proxy = os.environ.get("HTTPS_PROXY") or os.environ.get("HTTP_PROXY") if proxy: handler = urllib.request.ProxyHandler({"https": proxy}) opener = urllib.request.build_opener(handler) ``` 3. For MCP client config (Claude Desktop, Cursor): document proxy setup in troubleshooting ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] README troubleshooting section covers proxy setup - [ ]

We need a **fully conformant email address parser** in Python that implements the complete ABNF grammar from sections 3.2 through 3.4, plus obsolete syntax from §4.4. opportunities.title: Achievement rewards grant skins
opportunities.summary: ## Parent #104 ## What to build Make achievement rewards unlock durable cosmetics end to end. When a registered player earns a configured achievement from an authoritative completed game, grant the associated enabled skin in the same transaction. Return newly inserted grants to that player through the completed-game response, show the reward in the game-over experience, expose it in the authenticated cosmetics inventory, and allow it to be equipped through the existing controls. This slice establishes the server-authoritative unlock-rule catalog and shared transactional grant behavior used by later progression sources. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A migration can configure an enabled skin to be rewarded by a stable achievement ID. - [ ] Earning the configured achievement grants durable ownership in the same completed-game transaction. - [ ] One achievement may reward multiple skins without duplicating achievement ownership. - [ ] Only newly inserted ownership is reported as a new unlock. - [ ] A retried completed-game save does not duplicate stats, achievements, skin ownership, or the unlock announcement. - [ ] Disabled skins, invalid rules, guests, and bots receive no grant. - [ ]

opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
